Haematological disturbances including thrombocytopenia,1 eosinophilia,2 leucopenia, and, very rarely, pancytopenia,3 haemolytic anaemia,4 or agranulocytosis have been reported with ciprofloxacin and some other fluoroquinolo- nes. There has also been a case report5 of haemolytic-uraemic syndrome associated with ciprofloxacin therapy; the patient re- covered with routine supportive treatment (haemodialysis and plasma exchange) after the drug was stopped. In addition, tran- sient reductions in factor VIII and von Willebrand’s factor lead- ing to bleeding in 2 patients receiving ciprofloxacin has been re- ported.6 Neutropenia that developed in an elderly patient a few days after starting treatment with intravenous moxifloxacin re- solved on stopping the drug.7 1.
